audit_findings.title: FY2026 anchor may retain a nonrecurring $9.2 million government credit
audit_findings.magnitude: $9.2 million pretax, equal to 27.8% of the $33.1 million OE anchor
audit_findings.mechanism: If retained in FY2026 OE, the one-time credit raises the anchor and is propagated through every forecast year and terminal value.
audit_findings.evidence: During the years ended March 31, 2026 and 2025, we recorded $ 9.2 million and $ 0.5 million , respectively, of employee retention credits including associated interest received or expected to be received in cash as other (gains) charges, net, in the Consolidated Statements of Operations.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates that the credit was recorded in FY2026 operating results and that no further claims are expected. The record does not demonstrate whether the OE worksheet removed it. At 27.8% of the anchor before tax alignment, possible retention is material.
audit_findings.action: Trace the $9.2 million credit, associated interest, and $3.0 million receivable through the OE worksheet; remove the after-tax OE effect and rerun all scenarios and the buy-below price.

audit_findings.title: Anchor taxes may not reflect the imminent expiration of India's tax concession
audit_findings.magnitude: $4.1 million FY2026 SEZ benefit, equal to 12.4% of the $33.1 million OE anchor; $1.6 million minimum-alternative-tax credit
audit_findings.mechanism: The temporary concession increases anchor-period after-tax OE, while the forecast and terminal value require post-concession cash taxes.
audit_findings.evidence: The India subsidiary is then subject to 50 % of regular India income taxes during the second five years of operations which includes fiscal 2023 through fiscal 2027.
audit_findings.explanation: The concession's inclusion in FY2026 and its expiration after FY2027 are filed facts. The record does not show a post-expiration normalization. The disclosed $4.1 million benefit is large relative to the anchor, although the eventual recurring adjustment depends on taxable income and use of the $1.6 million credit.
audit_findings.action: Prepare a jurisdictional post-FY2027 cash-tax schedule, reconcile the $4.1 million benefit and $1.6 million credit, normalize forecast OE, and rerun all scenarios.

audit_findings.title: Gross cash may include customer advances that are not freely distributable excess cash
audit_findings.magnitude: potential adjustment unquantified; filed cash is $123.709 million and contract liabilities are $72.867 million
audit_findings.mechanism: The bridge adds all cash to operating value; any cash required to fulfill prepaid customer obligations or maintain operating liquidity is not excess cash available to equity holders.
audit_findings.evidence: Contract liabilities represent consideration received or consideration which is unconditionally due from customers prior to transferring goods or services to the customer under the terms of the contract.
audit_findings.explanation: The possible double count is unresolved because contract liabilities are not mechanically debt and projected OE may capture fulfillment costs and replacement advances. Nevertheless, contract liabilities equal 58.9% of added cash and 12.4% of base equity value, so the record cannot establish immateriality.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile cash by source and restriction, quantify required operating liquidity and fulfillment costs, confirm working-capital treatment in OE, and rerun the bridge using only demonstrably excess cash.

audit_findings.title: Capitalized sales commissions may escape the owner-earnings reinvestment charge
audit_findings.magnitude: $8.1 million capitalized balance; $2.3 million FY2026 net balance increase, equal to 6.9% of the $33.1 million OE anchor
audit_findings.mechanism: If OE adds back amortization or relies on GAAP expense without deducting current cash additions, recurring contract-acquisition spending is omitted from reinvestment and the anchor is overstated.
audit_findings.evidence: We had $ 8.1 million and $ 5.8 million of capitalized sales incentive costs as of March 31, 2026 and 2025, respectively.
audit_findings.explanation: The filings demonstrate recurring capitalization and a $2.3 million increase in the deferred-cost asset, but they do not disclose the OE worksheet treatment or a complete cash-additions roll-forward. The demonstrated net deferral is sufficiently large relative to the anchor to require a rerun.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the contract-cost roll-forward and cash additions, trace both current and non-current classifications into OE, deduct recurring cash additions without double-counting amortization, and rerun all scenarios.

audit_findings.title: Unfunded employee-benefit obligations are absent from the equity bridge
audit_findings.magnitude: $5.667 million maximum bridge claim, approximately $0.20 per diluted share and 1.0% of $589 million base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: Any economic cost not already captured through normalized employee-compensation expense would enter as a deduction in the equity bridge or as future OE cash payments.
audit_findings.evidence: Both the Gratuity and Leave Encashment Plans are unfunded with obligation amounts determined by actuarial valuations.
audit_findings.explanation: Even deducting the entire filed obligation, an intentionally conservative ceiling that ignores costs already recognized in OE, would reduce base value from $20.40 to about $20.20 per share. That scale cannot change the valuation conclusion relative to the $111.36 market price.
audit_findings.action: Confirm the latest obligation and expected payments are represented by normalized compensation expense; no valuation rerun is necessary unless the uncovered amount materially exceeds the filed $5.667 million obligation.

audit_findings.title: Foreign-exchange gains may be embedded in the latest OE anchor
audit_findings.magnitude: up to $3.894 million pretax, equal to 11.8% of the $33.1 million OE anchor before tax alignment
audit_findings.mechanism: A favorable currency gain included in OE raises the anchor and is capitalized through explicit forecasts and terminal value despite not representing sustainable operating cash generation.
audit_findings.evidence: Other income, net mainly consists of movement of foreign currencies against the U.S. dollar.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates $3.894 million of FY2026 other income and says the line mainly reflects currency movements. It does not establish the exact currency component or whether the OE worksheet removed it. The possible exposure is material relative to the anchor; the latest quarter's comparable line was only $0.153 million.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the FY2026 other-income ledger and OE reconciliation, separate transactional operating currency effects from nonrecurring remeasurement or translation gains, normalize the after-tax anchor, and rerun all scenarios.
